Holiday minutes, regular month
The weekend team met
Mei Hernandez and Ines Cohen were present, and Loki was also noted in the discussion. We opened with a quick run-through of the live board and the stack of animal travel files waiting on the Companion Animal Travel Desk. The main point was keeping safety ahead of speed on every booking, because one rushed handoff can turn into a problem fast. Staff were reminded to check crate fit, water access, carrier labels, and the comfort notes before anything is cleared for Aurelia Skyways.

We also talked through how service changes are being entered in the desk ledger, and everyone agreed that the notes need to stay clear, readable, and updated right away. A few recent cases showed that small changes can ripple across the trip if the record is not clean, so the desk will keep pushing for tighter handoffs between shifts. The team agreed to flag any odd paperwork at once instead of trying to smooth it over later.

There was a short review of traveler communication, especially for pet owners who arrive stressed and want fast answers. The team said calm wording helps, but we still need to be firm about required documents and safe transport standards. We also covered cage checks, cabin limits, and how to keep the waiting area moving without letting anything slip. The sense in the room was that routine work is holding steady, but only if we stay sharp and keep every note current.

The meeting ended with everyone clear on next steps and ready to keep the desk moving.
